findings.title: Error IDs are zipped against nodestore results in the wrong order
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `get_multi` gives back one value per input id, in input order. It doesn't. `NodeStorage.get_multi` (src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:184) dedupes the ids. It builds the result from the uncached ids and then does `items.update(cache_items)` (base.py:199-205), so cached entries end up after the uncached ones. If only some events are cached, or an id repeats, each error gets another event's title, message and timestamp, and Seer summarises the wrong data with no sign anything is off. Fix: look up each event by its own key, e.g. `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` takes `data["timestamp"]` from the error event in nodestore, which is a float in epoch seconds. `gen_request_data` compares it with the top-level rrweb `event.get("timestamp")`, which is in epoch milliseconds (the breadcrumb payload carries its own seconds timestamp; see `event["data"]["payload"]["timestamp"]` in event_parser.py:312). So `error_ts < event_ts` is always true. Every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb, and the chronological merge this change adds never takes effect. Convert one side to the other's unit before comparing, e.g. `error["timestamp"] * 1000`.

findings.title: Assemble analytics fires before the feature check
findings.body: The `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` event is recorded before `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)`. Requests that end in a 403 still count as assembles. If the metric is meant to count real assemble attempts, record it after the feature gate.

findings.title: Age/timestamp exclusivity checks use truthiness and accept reports with neither field
findings.body: `self.initial_data.get("age")` is falsy when `age` is 0, which the Editor's Draft allows, so a report with both `age: 0` and `timestamp` passes. A report with neither field also validates, because both fields are `required=False` and each validator only runs when its own field is present. Checking `"age" in self.initial_data` and requiring exactly one of the two in `validate()` would match the comment's intent.

findings.title: Hidden attributes still show when the search box is empty
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` is only checked inside the `.filter` on lines 65-69. When `searchQuery.trim()` is empty, the function returns `sorted` early on lines 61-63, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still appear in the default view. They only disappear once the user types something. Apply the hidden-attribute filter to `sorted` before the early return, for example `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`.

findings.title: Flex migration drops the gap and alignment the old FlexBox had
findings.body: The old `FlexBox` set `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)`, and `Container` added `justify-content: space-between` on top. `Flex` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:18-26) only emits the props it is given. So the second placeholder group (`<Flex>` on line 27) now has no gap and no centering, and its three placeholders render touching each other. The main container on line 93 (`<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">`) also loses `align-items: center` and `gap`, which shifts the tabs and vitals vertically. Add `align="center" gap={space(1)}` to both, as the first placeholder group on line 22 already does.

findings.title: Waterfall container loses `height: 100%`
findings.body: The removed `FlexBox` set `height: 100%` and `flex-grow: 1`. `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` sets neither a height nor anything equivalent (flex.tsx:18-26). If the parent is not a flex container along this axis, the waterfall no longer fills the available height. Check the trace page layout, or keep the height on a styled wrapper.

findings.title: Is it intended that attribute keys stop filtering by environment?
findings.body: Before this change the request sent `environment: selection.environments`. `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` now leaves it out ("environment left out intentionally as it's not supported"), and the query key no longer includes it, so changing the environment filter no longer refetches. The rewrite also drops `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false`, so the client defaults now apply. And `isLoading` now reports `isFetching`, so background refetches show as loading too. Did the endpoint ever honour `environment`, and are the retry and focus-refetch changes deliberate?

findings.title: Custom renderer results of 0 or '' fall back to the default renderer
findings.body: The prop docs and the story say only `undefined` triggers the fallback. But `if (cell)` (lines 32 and 71) also treats `0`, `''` and `null` as "not rendered". A custom renderer that returns `0` or an empty string is silently replaced by the default cell. Use `if (cell !== undefined)` to match the documented contract.

findings.title: "Project not found" can flash while projects are still loading
findings.body: `useProjectFromId` (static/app/utils/useProjectFromId.tsx:7-13) looks the id up in `useProjects().projects` and ignores the `fetching` state. If the projects store hasn't loaded yet, or the replay's project isn't in the user's loaded list yet, `project` is undefined and this branch shows a hard error instead of the loading indicator. Consider reading `fetching` from `useProjects()` and showing the error only after loading finishes.

findings.title: Tests no longer send the `application/reports+json` content type that browsers use
findings.body: Both success tests (`test_basic`, `test_handles_multiple_reports_both_specs`) used to post with `content_type="application/reports+json"`. Now they use the test client's default JSON format. The endpoint has a custom `BrowserReportsJSONParser` for that media type (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:63-82), and real browsers send it. After this change, no test covers that parser or the validation path reached through it. Keep at least one success case and one validation case on `application/reports+json`.

findings.title: Recording event timestamps in seconds hide a seconds-vs-milliseconds mismatch in the error interleaving
findings.body: The new tests give the rrweb event a top-level `timestamp` of `now.timestamp()`, which is in seconds (here and at line 254; `test_get_request_data` uses 1.5/2.0). In real recordings the top-level rrweb timestamp is in milliseconds, as the fixtures at `tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py:329` and `:363` show (`1674291701348`). `gen_request_data` (`src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:153-155`) compares the error's nodestore `timestamp` (seconds, from `fetch_error_details` at line 115) directly against `event.get("timestamp")`. With real millisecond data, every error is smaller than every event timestamp, so all errors get emitted before the first breadcrumb and the chronological ordering this feature promises silently fails. Because the tests use seconds on both sides, they pass and never catch it. Also, `test_get_with_error` only asserts `any(...)` membership, so it doesn't check ordering at all. Suggestion: build the segment events with millisecond timestamps, as real recordings have, and assert where the error line lands in `call_args["logs"]`. That test would fail until the endpoint normalizes the units.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** Part 1 has two real bugs in the new replay error context. Errors are paired with nodestore results by dict order, which is wrong when some events are cached or ids repeat. Error timestamps are in seconds but are compared with breadcrumb timestamps in milliseconds, so every error lands at the start of the log. Two smaller points: the preprod analytics event is recorded before the feature gate, and the browser-report age/timestamp checks use truthiness. I did not fully check whether the detector owner field (ActorField) validates that teams and users belong to the org.

**Batch 2 of 4.** I reviewed all 32 files in part 2 by reading them, not running them. Most of it is fine: the explore change from a list of y-axes to one `yAxis` per Visualize holds together across all the call sites I read. I found two defects to fix, both high confidence:
- **Hidden attributes still show** (`attributes.tsx:61`): in the trace drawer, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are only hidden while the user has typed a search. With an empty search box the code returns the full list before the hiding filter runs.
- **Layout regressions from the Flex migration** (`traceTabsAndVitals.tsx:27` and `:93`): the old wrapper set a gap and vertical centering, and the new `Flex` only applies the props it is given. The second group of loading placeholders now has no gap, and the tabs-and-vitals header is no longer vertically centred or spaced.

Three smaller points to consider:
- **Possible height loss** (`traceWaterfall.tsx:712`): the waterfall container no longer sets `height: 100%`. Whether that matters depends on the parent layout, which I didn't check.
- **Question on attribute keys** (`useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:30`): the request no longer sends the environment filter. It also stopped turning off retries and refetch-on-focus, and its loading flag now covers background refetches too. I'm asking whether each of these is intended.
- **Table renderer fallback** (`defaultTableCellRenderers.tsx:70`): the new table widget's cell renderers fall back to the default when a custom renderer returns `0` or `''`. The docs and story say only `undefined` should trigger the fallback.

**Batch 3 of 4.** Part 3 has no blockers and no defects that need a fix; I have two suggestions. Most of this part is mechanical: swapping styled divs for the shared `Flex` / `Flex.Item` components, and updating tests for the new `Visualize(yAxis)` signature (`fromJSON` now returns an array), the renamed `useGetTraceItemAttributeValues` hook, the new PR-comment format, the autofix default changing to "off", and `max_segment_id` being None. I checked each of these against the source and they match. Suggestion 1: the AI summary tab can briefly show "Project not found" while projects are still loading. Suggestion 2: the browser-reporting tests no longer use the `application/reports+json` content type that browsers send. Also, the PR body ("Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System") doesn't describe most of the changes in this part.

**Batch 4 of 4.** I reviewed all five test files in part 4 and found one issue, rated "consider" with medium confidence. The new replay tests write rrweb event timestamps in seconds. Real recordings use milliseconds (see `tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py:329`), so the tests hide a mismatch in the endpoint: it compares error timestamps in seconds with event timestamps in milliseconds, so every error lands before the first breadcrumb. The tests also only check that the error text is present, not where it appears in the log order. The other four files are fine. The detector owner tests match the validator and how `ActorField` checks organization membership. The delayed-workflow test changes match the new `dcg_to_slow_conditions` parameter. In the ourlogs top-N test, the expected counts are right: the top five groups are 60, 50, 40, 30 and 20, which leaves 10 for "Other".
